/.title: Observeri — AI-Powered GRC Platform | Cyber Risk Quantification
/.description: Observeri serves enterprises, SMEs, and startups worldwide. Cyber, technology, and operational risk combine into one view across regulatory regimes.
/.h1: AI-Powered GRC for Enterprises, SMEs, and Startups
body: Observeri is an AI-powered cybersecurity GRC platform and enterprise GRC solution built for enterprises, SMEs, and startups worldwide that need more than checkbox compliance. Our governance risk and compliance software unifies cyber risk management, IT risk management software workflows, and integrated risk management into a single AI Risk Operations Center — continuously scoring every asset, predicting risk exposure 30–90 days forward, and expressing residual risk as expected annual loss your board and CFO can act on.

Unlike legacy GRC platforms, Observeri is predictive, not retrospective. Our AI GRC platform for enterprises, SMEs, and startups in banking, energy, healthcare, government, and ports maps 3,000+ controls to SAMA, NESA, ISO 27001, NIST CSF, DORA, MiCA, and the EU AI Act — with deployment options including SaaS, KSA sovereign cloud, and hybrid on-premises. Replace your RSA Archer, ServiceNow IRM, or MetricStream implementation with a platform that compresses audit cycles without shelf-ware.

faqs.question: What is an AI GRC platform?
faqs.answer: An AI GRC platform uses artificial intelligence to automate governance, risk, and compliance workflows — continuously scoring assets, predicting risk exposure, and mapping controls to regulatory frameworks. Observeri's AI GRC platform goes further by expressing residual risk as expected annual loss rather than colour-coded heat maps.

faqs.question: How is Observeri different from RSA Archer or ServiceNow GRC?
faqs.answer: Observeri is AI-native and predictive. While Archer and ServiceNow record last quarter's assessments, Observeri forecasts risk exposure 30–90 days forward, quantifies risk in financial terms, and integrates external attack surface monitoring into the same risk register — enabling faster deployment and board-ready reporting.

faqs.question: Does Observeri support SAMA and NESA compliance?
faqs.answer: Yes. Observeri maps controls to SAMA Cybersecurity Framework and NESA requirements alongside global frameworks including ISO 27001, NIST CSF, DORA, and MiCA. The same coverage is available to enterprises, SMEs, and startups worldwide, including KSA sovereign cloud and hybrid deployment where data residency applies.

faqs.question: What deployment options does Observeri offer?
faqs.answer: Observeri supports SaaS, KSA sovereign cloud, and hybrid or on-premises (OVA) deployment, making it suitable for enterprises, SMEs, and startups worldwide, including organisations with data residency or sovereignty requirements.

faqs.question: How do cyber, operational, and financial risk sit together?
faqs.answer: Each domain keeps its own measure. Cyber risk uses expected annual loss, operational risk uses capital and loss events, and financial risk uses limits and regulatory capital. Together they augment one enterprise index.

faqs.question: What happens when control effectiveness changes?
faqs.answer: The updated rating is written back to the risk, the compliance record, and the incident the control maps to.

faqs.question: How does Observeri treat AI?
faqs.answer: Public and private models are inventoried and assessed, with a classification aid for the EU AI Act. Prompts and file uploads can be monitored, audited, or blocked.

faqs.question: What does internal audit include?
faqs.answer: The charter, the annual plan, the risk register, control assessment, reporting, capacity, and follow-up until the action closes.

/products/ai-risk-operations-center.title: AI Risk Operations Center | Continuous Predictive Risk Intelligence
/products/ai-risk-operations-center.description: Observeri's AI Risk Operations Center continuously re-scores every asset, forecasts risk 30–90 days forward, and expresses exposure as expected annual loss. One intelligence engine for all risk signals.
/products/ai-risk-operations-center.h1: AI Risk Operations Center — One Intelligence Engine for Every Risk Signal
body: The AI Risk Operations Center is Observeri's core intelligence layer. It consolidates incidents, risks, vulnerabilities, threats, and compliance issues into a single operational view — calculating a live asset risk score for every asset and directing your team to where remediation protects the highest-value targets.

Unlike periodic GRC assessments, the AI Risk Operations Center operates continuously. As new signals arrive — a new CVE, a change in control effectiveness, a vendor breach — scores update automatically. Predictive AI models forecast risk exposure 30–90 days forward, enabling CISOs and risk owners to shift from reactive response to proactive resilience. Risk is expressed as expected annual loss, not red/amber/green, so executives and CFOs can fund remediation against a financial risk appetite.

faqs.question: What is an AI Risk Operations Center?
faqs.answer: An AI Risk Operations Center (AI ROC) is a continuous intelligence engine that aggregates cyber, technology, operational, and compliance risk signals and uses AI to score, prioritise, and forecast exposure in real time — replacing periodic, manual risk assessments with always-on risk intelligence.

faqs.question: How does Observeri's AI ROC differ from a traditional GRC dashboard?
faqs.answer: A traditional GRC dashboard records past assessments. Observeri's AI ROC continuously re-scores assets as signals change and predicts exposure 30–90 days forward, expressed as expected annual loss — giving boards and CISOs a financial view of risk rather than static colour ratings.

faqs.question: Which risk types does the AI Risk Operations Center cover?
faqs.answer: The AI ROC covers cyber risk, technology risk, operational risk, third-party and vendor risk, AI model risk, and compliance risk — all on a unified taxonomy and a single risk register.

/products/enterprise-risk.title: Enterprise Risk Index, Appetite, and War Rooms | Observeri
/products/enterprise-risk.description: Roll every risk domain into one global index, with taxonomy, appetite, KRIs, limits, breach response, board packs, and live war rooms.
/products/enterprise-risk.h1: Enterprise Risk — One Index Across Every Domain
body: Observeri Enterprise Risk lets the organisation define the taxonomy, appetite, matrix, limits, enterprise KRIs, and workflows. Every domain augments one global risk index. Each threshold carries the response designed for that breach, and a critical risk opens a real-time war room.

Cyber, financial, reputational, operational, compliance, AI, geopolitical, supply chain, and ESG and technology keep their own position. Board-ready packs take the index, the heatmap, and the patterns that cross those domains.

faqs.question: What is the global risk index?
faqs.answer: The global risk index is the combined position of every risk domain. Each domain keeps its own score and direction, and those domains augment the single enterprise index.

faqs.question: What can the enterprise define?
faqs.answer: The enterprise defines the risk taxonomy, risk appetite, risk matrix, risk limits, enterprise KRIs, and workflows. Each threshold also holds the response designed for that breach.

faqs.question: What is a war room?
faqs.answer: A war room is a real-time view opened on a critical risk. It stays on that risk, with the domains, indicators, and actions moving it, until the risk is no longer critical.

/products/financial-risk.title: Financial Risk Limits and Capital Impact | Observeri
/products/financial-risk.description: Monitor capital, market, and liquidity risks against organisation-defined limits, with early warning, breach escalation, and regulatory capital impact.
/products/financial-risk.h1: Financial Risk — Limits, Breaches, and Regulatory Capital
body: Observeri Financial Risk keeps capital, market, liquidity, and credit risks on one register. Each risk is tested against the limits the organisation defines, from within limit through early warning to breach, and the regulatory capital impact stays on that record.
A limit shows its threshold, reading, and utilisation, and it is tested on its taxonomy node and on every node above it. When a warning or a breach opens, the escalation path is already named.

faqs.question: Which financial risks are on the register?
faqs.answer: The register covers capital, market, liquidity, and credit risks, scored on one taxonomy and the organisation's appetite.

faqs.question: How are risks monitored against limits?
faqs.answer: Each limit has a threshold the organisation sets, a current reading, and a utilisation. Status moves among within limit, early warning, hard breach, and severe. A risk is tested against its own limit and every limit above it.

faqs.question: Where does regulatory capital impact appear?
faqs.answer: The regulatory capital impact sits on the same limit as the reading. A warning or a breach does not wait for a separate capital pack to explain the consequence.

/products/operational-risk.title: Operational Risk Management and Capital | Observeri
/products/operational-risk.description: Run operational risk end to end: RCSA, live KRIs on each risk, loss events, operational capital, and back-testing under Pillar 1 and Pillar 2.
/products/operational-risk.h1: Operational Risk — Assess, Indicate, Quantify, and Back-Test
body: Observeri Operational Risk runs the assessment end to end: RCSA, key risk indicators mapped to each risk, loss events, and operational capital. Quantification follows a Pillar 1 minimum-capital view and a Pillar 2 internal view, then back-tests both against the losses that occurred.

Each risk keeps its business unit, inherent and residual scores, and appetite position. A KRI breach and a new loss event show on that risk, and capital monitoring moves with them instead of waiting for the next workshop.

faqs.question: What does the operational risk assessment include?
faqs.answer: The assessment records the risk, the business unit, inherent and residual scores, appetite position, and the treatment. RCSA is how the owning unit assesses the risk and its controls, and that result updates the same record.

faqs.question: How are KRIs mapped to a risk?
faqs.answer: Each key risk indicator is attached to the operational risk it describes. When the indicator crosses a threshold, the breach is shown on that risk rather than on a separate dashboard.

faqs.question: How do Pillar 1, Pillar 2, and back-testing fit together?
faqs.answer: Pillar 1 is the minimum operational-risk capital view. Pillar 2 is the firm's own capital view against its risk profile and appetite, and it can sit above the Pillar 1 minimum. Back-testing compares those figures with recorded loss events.

/products/cyber-risk-management.title: Cyber Risk Management Software | AI Quantification & Predictive Scoring
/products/cyber-risk-management.description: Observeri cyber risk management software connects risks to live controls and assets, updates scores continuously, and quantifies exposure as expected annual loss. Act on the risk that matters most.
/products/cyber-risk-management.h1: Cyber Risk Management Software — Quantify, Predict, and Remediate with Precision
body: Observeri GRC connects risks to live controls, assets, and signals — updating scores as your security posture changes and giving your team a clear, prioritised view of what to tackle next. As a cyber risk quantification software platform, Observeri moves beyond subjective ratings by expressing exposure as expected annual loss using FAIR-aligned financial modelling.

The predictive cyber risk platform forecasts exploitability and risk exposure 30–90 days forward, so remediation follows financial impact — not noise in the vulnerability queue. Board-level cyber risk reporting is built in: executives see their risk in dollars, not heat maps, enabling faster budget approvals and more credible governance conversations. For organisations replacing RSA Archer, ServiceNow IRM, or MetricStream, Observeri deploys faster, requires less customisation, and delivers quantified cyber risk insight from day one.

faqs.question: What is cyber risk quantification?
faqs.answer: Cyber risk quantification (CRQ) is the process of expressing cybersecurity risk in financial terms — typically as expected annual loss (EAL) or loss exceedance curves — so organisations can prioritise investment and communicate risk to boards and CFOs in language they understand.

faqs.question: How does Observeri quantify cyber risk?
faqs.answer: Observeri uses a FAIR-aligned approach: asset value multiplied by threat probability and residual control effectiveness produces an expected annual loss figure. This updates continuously as new signals arrive, giving live financial risk exposure rather than a point-in-time assessment.

faqs.question: Can Observeri replace RSA Archer for cyber risk management?
faqs.answer: Yes. Observeri is an AI-native alternative to RSA Archer for cyber risk management. It deploys faster, requires no complex customisation, and delivers predictive risk quantification and board-ready financial reporting that Archer does not offer natively.

/products/ai-governance.title: AI Governance for Public and Private Models | Observeri
/products/ai-governance.description: Inventory public and private AI models and govern each system through the seven ISO/IEC 22989:2022 life cycle stages, from inception to retirement.
/products/ai-governance.h1: AI Governance — Inventory Every Model and Run Its Life Cycle
body: Observeri AI Governance keeps one inventory of public and private AI models and moves each system through the ISO/IEC 22989:2022 life cycle: inception, design and development, verification and validation, deployment, operation and monitoring, re-evaluation, and retirement.

Owners, purpose, data, and hosting stay on the model record. When a system keeps learning in production, continuous validation runs inside operation and monitoring. A model does not change stage without evidence, and retirement includes access removal and data disposal.

faqs.question: Which models belong in the AI inventory?
faqs.answer: The inventory covers public models, including foundation models and vendor APIs, and private models, including fine-tunes and internal deployments. Each record stores purpose, owner, data, hosting, and the current life cycle stage.

faqs.question: What are the seven ISO/IEC 22989:2022 life cycle stages?
faqs.answer: Observeri governs models through inception, design and development, verification and validation, deployment, operation and monitoring, re-evaluation, and retirement. ISO/IEC 22989:2022 also names continuous validation for systems that keep learning; that work runs inside operation and monitoring.

faqs.question: How does retirement work?
faqs.answer: Retirement decommissions or replaces the model, removes access, and records disposal of training data, prompts, and uploaded files so a closed model cannot still be used.

/products/ai-data-monitoring.title: AI Data Monitoring for Prompts and Uploads | Observeri
/products/ai-data-monitoring.description: Monitor and audit AI prompts on sanctioned tools, block sensitive prompts and file uploads, and keep protected information inside the organization.
/products/ai-data-monitoring.h1: AI Data Monitoring — See, Audit, and Block Prompts and Uploads
body: Observeri AI Data Monitoring watches prompts and file uploads on sanctioned AI tools. Sensitive prompts are audited and blocked before they reach a model outside the organization, so secrets, personal data, and other protected information stay inside.

The audit trail records who prompted, which model was targeted, and which policy matched. Findings are stored without making a second copy of the sensitive value, and blocks are available to AI governance for review.

faqs.question: What does prompt monitoring cover?
faqs.answer: Prompt monitoring covers sanctioned public and private AI tools. Each event records the user, the tool, the model, and whether a policy matched the prompt or an attached file.

faqs.question: Can prompts and file uploads be blocked?
faqs.answer: Yes. Prompts and file uploads that contain secrets, personal data, or other sensitive content are blocked before they leave the organization. The person sees the block, and the event is kept for audit.

faqs.question: Does the audit log store the sensitive data?
faqs.answer: The audit record stores the actor, time, destination model, and the policy that matched. It records the finding without keeping another copy of the protected value.

/products/ai-risk.title: AI Model Risk Management for the EU AI Act | Observeri
/products/ai-risk.description: Inventory public and private AI models, run STRIDE assessments, apply suggested controls, and treat risk with automatic EU AI Act classification.
/products/ai-risk.h1: AI Risk Management — Inventory, Assess, and Treat Every Model
body: Observeri AI Risk keeps a live inventory of public and private AI models, then runs an end-to-end assessment: STRIDE threat models, AI-suggested controls, and a recorded risk treatment. Each model is classified automatically against the EU AI Act so owners know the obligations before a model reaches production.

Security, risk, and compliance teams work from one register instead of scattered model lists. Public foundation models and vendor APIs sit beside private fine-tunes and internal deployments, with purpose, data, owners, and residual risk kept current as the estate changes.

faqs.question: What does the AI model inventory cover?
faqs.answer: The inventory covers public models, such as foundation models and vendor APIs, and private models, such as fine-tunes and internal deployments. Each record stores purpose, owner, data sources, hosting, and the current EU AI Act classification.

faqs.question: How does STRIDE apply to AI models?
faqs.answer: Observeri applies STRIDE — spoofing, tampering, repudiation, information disclosure, denial of service, and elevation of privilege — across the model, its training and prompt data, integrations, and the people who operate it.

faqs.question: How are models classified under the EU AI Act?
faqs.answer: Observeri classifies each model from its intended purpose and use context into the EU AI Act tiers: prohibited, high-risk, limited-risk transparency obligations, or minimal risk. Classification updates when purpose or deployment changes. It supports compliance work and is not a legal determination.

/products/audit-management.title: Audit Management Software for Internal Audit | Observeri
/products/audit-management.description: Cover the audit charter, engagement planning, the risk register, control assessment, reporting, resource capacity, and follow-up in one audit workspace.
body: Connect the charter, the annual plan, fieldwork, control testing, reporting, and follow-up so assurance advises the business and the action stays attached.
Observeri keeps engagements on one record from planning through reporting. Findings stay open in the follow-up tracker until the action closes, and hours and budget sit on the same plan as the work.

faqs.question: What is Observeri internal audit management?
faqs.answer: It is the internal audit workspace for the charter, annual plan, engagements, audit risk register, control assessment, reporting, resource and capacity planning, and the follow-up tracker.

faqs.question: What does the audit charter cover?
faqs.answer: The charter records the purpose of internal audit, its authority, its independence, and its scope. Engagements inherit that mandate instead of restating it in a separate document.

faqs.question: How does risk information flow into the audit plan?
faqs.answer: The annual plan and each engagement are linked to the audit risks that justify them. When a risk changes, the engagement that addresses it stays visible on the same record.

faqs.question: How are audit hours and capacity tracked?
faqs.answer: Resource and capacity planning shows planned hours, hours used, and budget utilization for the year and for each engagement, before the work is already overdue.

faqs.question: How does control testing work inside an engagement?
faqs.answer: Auditors test design and operating effectiveness on the engagement, record exceptions, and rate effectiveness next to the finding, the rating, and the owner.

faqs.question: What does audit reporting include?
faqs.answer: Reporting records each finding with a risk level and an owner, and assembles the report that management and the audit committee receive from the same engagement.

faqs.question: What happens after a finding is reported?
faqs.answer: The finding stays on the follow-up tracker with its owner, due date, and closure evidence. Reporting does not end the engagement; the action remains open until it is closed.

/products/budget-management.title: Budget Management for Risk-Led Investment | Observeri
/products/budget-management.description: Compare the cost of impact with the cost of mitigation so every investment dollar is driven by risk and compliance, and the board can decide what to fund.
/products/budget-management.h1: Budget Management — Compare Cost of Impact with Cost of Mitigation
body: Every dollar of investment is driven by a risk or a compliance obligation. The board sees the cost of impact beside the cost of mitigation, then funds, defers, or accepts on that comparison.

The cost of impact is the loss, or the exposure from a missed obligation, if nothing is spent. The cost of mitigation is what the control, project, or programme costs. The decision stays on the same record as the residual impact.

faqs.question: What drives an investment decision?
faqs.answer: Each dollar is attached to a risk or a compliance obligation. The board compares the cost of impact with the cost of mitigation before it funds, defers, or accepts the investment.

faqs.question: What is the cost of impact?
faqs.answer: The cost of impact is the expected loss, or the exposure from a missed compliance obligation, if the investment is not made.

faqs.question: What is the cost of mitigation?
faqs.answer: The cost of mitigation is what the control, project, or programme costs to reduce that impact.

faqs.question: What does the board record?
faqs.answer: The board records fund, defer, or accept. When the dollar is not spent, the residual impact stays on the same record as the decision.

/products/security-governance.title: Security Governance Platform | ISO 27001, NIST CSF & Control Mapping
/products/security-governance.description: Observeri Security Governance unifies KRI/KPI monitoring, policy management, automated control assessment, and change management — giving CISOs one workspace to steer the security programme.
/products/security-governance.h1: Security Governance Platform — Govern Security with Evidence, Not Estimates
body: Observeri Security Governance unifies KRI/KPI monitoring, policy management, AI budgeting, change management, and dedicated project management — giving boards and CISOs one workspace to steer the security programme with defensible evidence.

As a cybersecurity governance software platform, Observeri pre-maps 3,000+ controls to ISO 27001, NIST CSF, SAMA, NESA, SOC 2, and other frameworks, with automated control assessment that tests design and operating effectiveness continuously. GRC control mapping is automated — eliminating the manual spreadsheet work that slows down traditional governance cycles. Observeri serves enterprises, SMEs, and startups worldwide, and covers the regulatory regimes they work under, from regional standards to global ones.

faqs.question: What is a security governance platform?
faqs.answer: A security governance platform provides the tools CISOs and security teams need to manage policies, monitor key risk and performance indicators, map controls to frameworks, and demonstrate compliance to boards and regulators — replacing fragmented spreadsheets and manual processes.

faqs.question: Does Observeri support ISO 27001 control mapping?
faqs.answer: Yes. Observeri pre-maps 3,000+ controls to ISO 27001 and automates both design and operating effectiveness testing, producing audit-ready evidence without manual documentation effort.

faqs.question: Which governance frameworks does Observeri support?
faqs.answer: Observeri supports ISO 27001, NIST CSF, NIST 800-53, SAMA Cybersecurity Framework, NESA, SOC 2, DORA, MiCA, EU AI Act, and ISO 42001, with the ability to add custom frameworks and cross-map controls across multiple standards simultaneously.

/products/external-attack-surface-manage.title: External Attack Surface Management (EASM) | Continuous Attack Surface Monitoring
/products/external-attack-surface-manage.description: Observeri EASM continuously discovers, scans, and prioritises every public-facing asset — domains, cloud services, shadow IT, dark-web signals — so security teams close exposure before attackers find it.
/products/external-attack-surface-manage.h1: External Attack Surface Management — Know Every Edge of Your Exposure Before Attackers Do
body: Observeri EASM discovers internet-facing hosts and the vulnerabilities on them, then runs penetration testing, shadow IT review, and attack simulation. It also finds external APIs and third parties, monitors the dark web and public social channels, reviews blockchain assets, and uses an AI ethical hacker to show which of your hosts are breachable.

For most enterprises, the known perimeter is a myth. Shadow IT, dormant subdomains, and unsanctioned SaaS expand faster than manual inventories can track. Observeri EASM integrated with GRC platform workflows means every discovered asset feeds directly into the same risk register, control mapping, and remediation workflow — unlike standalone EASM tools that exist in a separate scanner silo. Dark web monitoring, social mentions, external APIs, third parties, and blockchain findings sit on that same record.

faqs.question: What is External Attack Surface Management (EASM)?
faqs.answer: EASM is the continuous discovery, monitoring, and prioritisation of an organisation's internet-facing assets — everything visible and potentially reachable by an attacker, including shadow IT, forgotten subdomains, misconfigured cloud services, and exposed APIs.

faqs.question: How is Observeri EASM different from a vulnerability scanner?
faqs.answer: A vulnerability scanner tests known assets you tell it about. Observeri EASM discovers assets you may not know exist, continuously monitors them for new exposures, and integrates findings directly into the GRC risk register — so discovered risk immediately informs governance and remediation workflows.

faqs.question: Does Observeri EASM include dark web monitoring?
faqs.answer: Yes. Dark web monitoring surfaces mentions of the organisation, its domains, and exposed data. The finding records the signal. It does not keep a second copy of the secret.

faqs.question: What does the AI ethical hacker show?
faqs.answer: It tests the organisation's own internet-facing hosts and records which ones it can show are breachable. The result is a finding on the host for the team to close. The demonstration does not publish the method.

faqs.question: What else does external discovery cover?
faqs.answer: Besides hosts and vulnerabilities, discovery covers external APIs, third parties on the footprint, public social mentions, and blockchain assets linked to those hosts.

/products/information-asset-management.title: Information Asset Management | AI-Powered Asset Risk Scoring & Inventory
/products/information-asset-management.description: Observeri Information Asset Management ingests assets via API or ETL, assigns live AI risk scores from the AI ROC, and gives teams a unified exposure graph to prioritise remediation on what matters most.
/products/information-asset-management.h1: Information Asset Management — Every Asset Scored, Every Control Measured
body: Observeri Information Asset Management ingests assets through API, ETL, or manual entry — then pulls live AI risk scores and control effectiveness data from the AI Risk Operations Center. Teams explore a unified exposure graph, drill into CIA triad impact, and prioritise remediation on the assets that carry the greatest business risk.

As an information asset management software platform built for enterprises, SMEs, and startups worldwide, Observeri maintains a live information asset register that feeds directly into ISO 27001 control mapping, risk assessments, and audit workflows. Asset-based risk quantification means every remediation decision is backed by financial exposure data — not subjective criticality ratings. Technology asset classification for enterprises, SMEs, and startups worldwide is built in, with deployment-ready integrations for common asset sources including cloud platforms, CMDB tools, and vulnerability scanners.

faqs.question: What is information asset management in GRC?
faqs.answer: Information asset management in GRC is the practice of discovering, classifying, and continuously scoring an organisation's information assets — systems, data, applications, and infrastructure — against their risk exposure, so remediation and control investment follows business value.

faqs.question: How does Observeri score asset risk?
faqs.answer: Observeri uses its AI Risk Operations Center to continuously calculate a live risk score for each asset, combining asset value, CIA triad impact, control effectiveness, threat probability, and exploitability signals — updating automatically as conditions change.

faqs.question: Does the asset management module support ISO 27001 requirements?
faqs.answer: Yes. Observeri's information asset register is designed to meet ISO 27001 asset management requirements (Annex A.5.9 and A.5.10), with automated classification, ownership assignment, and evidence output ready for audit.

/products/data-privacy-protection.title: Data Privacy & AI Data Loss Prevention | AI DLP Platform for Enterprises
/products/data-privacy-protection.description: Observeri detects, classifies, and scores sensitive data across every connected source. AI data loss prevention for enterprises, SMEs, and startups worldwide.
/products/data-privacy-protection.h1: Data Privacy & Protection — Find Sensitive Data. Classify It. Score the Exposure.
body: Observeri Data Privacy & Protection delivers PII detection and classification, sensitive data discovery, secret and credential scanning, NER-based identification, data exposure scoring, and unified classification across every connected source — so privacy teams know what data exists, where it lives, and how exposed it is.

As an AI data loss prevention platform, Observeri monitors AI model data governance in real time, detecting data leakage from open and self-hosted AI models before it becomes a breach. For enterprises, SMEs, and startups working under UAE PDPL, Saudi PDPL, the EU AI Act, ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF, and the other regimes they follow, Observeri's AI DLP combines traditional data privacy management with AI-specific governance — closing the gap that legacy DLP tools leave open when employees use LLMs with sensitive data.

faqs.question: What is AI DLP and how is it different from traditional DLP?
faqs.answer: Traditional DLP monitors known data flows across defined channels. AI DLP extends this to monitor how sensitive data interacts with AI models — detecting when employees share PII, credentials, or confidential information with LLMs like ChatGPT or Copilot, and preventing data leakage through AI prompts and outputs.

faqs.question: Does Observeri support UAE and Saudi data privacy law compliance?
faqs.answer: Yes. Observeri supports compliance with the UAE Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL) and Saudi Arabia's PDPL, providing data discovery, classification, and exposure scoring capabilities aligned to both regulatory frameworks.

faqs.question: How does Observeri detect AI model data leakage?
faqs.answer: Observeri monitors data flows to and from AI models in real time using NER (Named Entity Recognition) and classification models that identify sensitive data types — flagging and optionally blocking interactions that risk exposing PII, credentials, or confidential business data.

/products/data-loss-prevention.title: Data Loss Prevention and Shadow Channels | Observeri
/products/data-loss-prevention.description: Observeri DLP approves email, cloud drive, and AI tools, catches shadow mediums, and turns a blocked or audited violation into a risk incident.
/products/data-loss-prevention.h1: Data Loss Prevention — Approved Channels, Caught Shadow Mediums
body: Observeri Data Loss Prevention starts with the channels the organisation approves: email service providers, cloud drive providers, and AI models. When someone uses a medium outside that list, the system catches the shadow use.

Teams define the infotypes that matter and the policies that act on them. A policy can block, audit keywords, or audit files, and it sends the violation. From that violation, the team opens a risk incident.

faqs.question: Which channels does the organisation approve first?
faqs.answer: The organisation lists the email service providers, cloud drive providers, and AI models that are allowed. Policies and shadow detection are measured against that list.

faqs.question: What happens when someone uses a shadow medium?
faqs.answer: A shadow medium is an email service, cloud drive, or AI model outside the approved list. When someone uses it, the system catches that use, including a tool that had gone dormant.

faqs.question: How does a violation become a risk incident?
faqs.answer: Infotypes and policies decide whether a match is blocked, audited, or warned. The violation is sent with the tool, the time, and the outcome, and the team can convert that violation into a risk incident.

/products/centralised-controls-managemen.title: Centralised Controls Management and Testing | Observeri
/products/centralised-controls-managemen.description: Observeri keeps 3,000+ controls, approves applicability, tests with evidence, rates effectiveness, and updates mapped risk, compliance, and incidents.
/products/centralised-controls-managemen.h1: Centralised Controls — Library, Testing, and Live Effectiveness
body: Observeri Centralised Controls Management holds a library of more than 3,000 controls. The organisation approves which controls apply, and users test those controls through a workflow, upload the evidence, and rate control effectiveness.
When effectiveness is updated, every risk, compliance item, and incident the control maps to updates with it. The mapped records read the current rating instead of a copy from the last review.

faqs.question: How does the organisation choose which controls apply?
faqs.answer: The controls library is an inventory of more than 3,000 controls. The organisation approves applicability on each control, and only an applicable control enters the testing workflow.

faqs.question: How is a control tested and rated?
faqs.answer: Users perform the test through a workflow, upload the evidence to that test, and rate the control effectiveness. The rating becomes the current score on the control.

faqs.question: What updates when control effectiveness changes?
faqs.answer: Every risk, compliance item, and incident the control maps to updates automatically with the new effectiveness. Those records do not keep the previous rating.

/products/automated-compliance.title: Automated Compliance for On-Prem and Cloud | Observeri
/products/automated-compliance.description: Observeri on-prem agent for Windows and Linux, virtual connector for Azure, GCP, AWS, and Oracle Cloud, scheduled checks, and a real-time risk view.
/products/automated-compliance.h1: Automated Compliance — On-Prem, Cloud, and a Live Risk View
body: Observeri Automated Compliance runs from an on-prem agent on Windows and Linux, and from a virtual connector on Azure, GCP, AWS, and Oracle Cloud. The organisation schedules the assessment so posture is checked on a cadence.
Each run updates the posture of the on-prem and cloud stack. The result is a real-time risk view of the environments the organisation actually runs.

faqs.question: Where does the on-prem agent run?
faqs.answer: The on-prem agent runs automated compliance on Windows and Linux environments inside the organisation's own network.

faqs.question: Which clouds does the virtual connector cover?
faqs.answer: The virtual connector runs compliance on Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, Amazon Web Services, and Oracle Cloud, on the same assessment as the on-prem agent.

faqs.question: How does the organisation get a real-time risk view?
faqs.answer: Users schedule the assessment for the on-prem stack, the cloud stack, or both. As each check finishes, the risk view of that posture updates.

/products/business-continuity-management.title: Business Continuity, BIA, and Crisis Rooms | Observeri
/products/business-continuity-management.description: Observeri keeps a BIA register, ties DR and BCP plans to it, runs a crisis war room for live decisions, and simulates the whole BCP and DR exercise.
/products/business-continuity-management.h1: Business Continuity — BIA, Plans, War Room, and Exercises
body: Observeri Business Continuity Management is where the organisation creates and maintains the business impact analysis register, and keeps disaster recovery and business continuity plans tied to that register.

Crisis management runs in a war room, with actions and decisions taken in real time. Teams conduct BCP and DR exercises, and they can simulate the whole exercise from the first impact through the last decision.

faqs.question: What does the BIA register hold?
faqs.answer: The register is the business impact analysis: the processes, what they depend on, and the impact if they stop. Users create it and keep it current. DR and BCP plans are tied to the entries in it.

faqs.question: How does the war room work in a crisis?
faqs.answer: Crisis management opens a war room on the event. Actions and decisions are taken there in real time, and they stay on the record of that crisis.

faqs.question: Can an exercise simulate the whole event?
faqs.answer: Yes. Teams conduct BCP and DR exercises against the plans, and they can simulate the whole exercise, from the impact through the plan, the war room, and the decisions.

/products/third-party-risk.title: Third-Party Risk Management Software | Vendor Risk & Nth-Party Visibility
/products/third-party-risk.description: Observeri autonomously maintains a live vendor risk profile for every third party, with continuous monitoring, automated assessments, and Nth-party visibility — integrated with the same GRC risk register.
/products/third-party-risk.h1: Third-Party Risk Management — Your Vendors. Their Exposure. Your Responsibility.
body: Observeri GRC autonomously maintains a live inventory and risk profile for every vendor, so you can answer one question at any time: are we safe to depend on them right now? As a third-party risk management software platform, Observeri automates vendor onboarding, questionnaire distribution, ongoing monitoring, and Nth-party visibility — all tied to the same control and issue workflows as your internal risk register.

For banking and financial services organisations subject to DORA third-party ICT risk requirements and SAMA outsourcing risk guidelines, Observeri provides the continuous vendor monitoring software needed to evidence compliance without manual spreadsheet tracking. Automated vendor risk questionnaires, real-time scoring updates, and Nth-party risk management platform capabilities give risk teams full supply chain visibility — from direct suppliers to the vendors their vendors rely on.

faqs.question: What is third-party risk management?
faqs.answer: Third-party risk management (TPRM) is the process of identifying, assessing, and continuously monitoring the cyber, operational, and compliance risks introduced by vendors, suppliers, and other external parties — including Nth-party risks from the vendors your vendors use.

faqs.question: How does Observeri handle DORA third-party ICT risk requirements?
faqs.answer: Observeri maps vendor risk assessments and monitoring to DORA's ICT third-party risk requirements, automating questionnaire distribution, criticality classification, ongoing monitoring, and incident notification workflows for regulated financial institutions.

faqs.question: What is Nth-party risk and how does Observeri address it?
faqs.answer: Nth-party risk refers to the risk introduced by the vendors of your vendors — suppliers two or more tiers down your supply chain. Observeri's Nth-party visibility layer maps these relationships and surfaces risk signals from across the supply chain, not just your direct vendors.

/products/vulnerability-operations.title: Vulnerability Operations Platform | Exploit-Ranked Risk-Based Vulnerability Management
/products/vulnerability-operations.description: Observeri ingests vulnerability findings, enriches every CVE with exploit context, and prioritises remediation by real-world exploitability and business impact — not CVSS scores alone.
/products/vulnerability-operations.h1: Vulnerability Operations — Prioritise What Is Exploitable. Fix What Matters First.
body: Observeri Vulnerability Operations ingests findings from APIs or Excel, enriches every CVE with exploit context, prioritises with an exploitability agent, tracks SLAs, and converts the highest-impact issues into managed remediation programmes.

As a risk-based vulnerability management platform, Observeri moves beyond CVSS-only prioritisation. Exploit-prioritised vulnerability remediation means teams focus on vulnerabilities with active exploits in the wild — not the longest list of theoretical findings. AI vulnerability risk scoring combines asset value, business context, control effectiveness, and threat intelligence to produce a ranked remediation queue that security engineers and GRC teams can both use. Vulnerability management integrated with GRC means every finding flows into the same risk register, control mapping, and audit trail.

faqs.question: What is risk-based vulnerability management?
faqs.answer: Risk-based vulnerability management (RBVM) prioritises vulnerabilities by their actual risk to the business — considering exploitability, asset value, business context, and control effectiveness — rather than ranking purely by CVSS severity scores, which often misrepresent real-world risk.

faqs.question: How does Observeri prioritise vulnerability remediation?
faqs.answer: Observeri uses an exploitability agent that enriches every CVE with real-world exploit intelligence, then combines this with asset value, control effectiveness, and business impact to produce a ranked remediation queue. SLA tracking ensures high-priority findings receive timely attention.

faqs.question: What is the difference between CVSS and exploit-based scoring?
faqs.answer: CVSS (Common Vulnerability Scoring System) rates vulnerability severity based on technical characteristics. Exploit-based scoring additionally considers whether an exploit is actively used in the wild, making it a more accurate predictor of real breach risk and enabling more focused remediation effort.

/products/exposure-management.title: Exposure Management Platform | Continuous Threat Exposure Management (CTEM)
/products/exposure-management.description: Observeri Exposure Management unifies assessment planning, issue tracking, remediation, EASM, and AI threat analysis — so teams reduce exposure from the perimeter to the core with precision.
/products/exposure-management.h1: Exposure Management — See Your Full Exposure. Close It with Precision.
body: Observeri Exposure Management unifies assessment planning, centralised issue tracking, a dedicated remediation hub, external attack surface visibility, and AI-powered threat analysis — so teams plan tests, prioritise findings, and reduce exposure from the perimeter to the core.

As a continuous threat exposure management (CTEM) platform — aligned to the Gartner CTEM framework — Observeri provides the structured programme enterprises need to move from ad hoc vulnerability scanning to systematic, measurable exposure reduction. CTEM vs EASM: exposure management goes further than surface monitoring, encompassing the full cycle of scoping, discovery, prioritisation, validation, and mobilisation. Attack surface exposure scoring gives security and GRC teams a unified view of where the organisation is most at risk, with GRC-integrated exposure management ensuring every finding feeds the risk register and compliance workflows.

faqs.question: What is Continuous Threat Exposure Management (CTEM)?
faqs.answer: CTEM is a Gartner-defined framework for continuous, programmatic reduction of cyber exposure. It covers five stages — scoping, discovery, prioritisation, validation, and mobilisation — and shifts organisations from periodic assessments to always-on exposure reduction.

faqs.question: What is the difference between CTEM and EASM?
faqs.answer: EASM (External Attack Surface Management) focuses on discovering and monitoring internet-facing assets. CTEM is broader — it encompasses the full exposure reduction programme, including internal assets, vulnerability validation, and the organisational processes that turn findings into fixed risk. Observeri integrates both.

faqs.question: Why is exposure management important?
faqs.answer: Regulators increasingly expect organisations to demonstrate continuous, evidence-based risk reduction — not just annual assessments. A CTEM platform provides the structured programme, audit trail, and quantified exposure metrics needed to satisfy SAMA, NESA, DORA, and ISO 27001 requirements.

/products/compliance-management.title: Compliance Management Software | SAMA, NESA, ISO 27001, DORA — Multi-Framework GRC
/products/compliance-management.description: Observeri automates multi-framework compliance — building registers from regulations, running AI self-assessments, tracking submissions, and managing incidents — across SAMA, NESA, ISO 27001, DORA, and more.
/products/compliance-management.h1: Compliance Management — From Regulation to Evidence. Compliance That Runs Itself.
body: Observeri Compliance Management lets teams maintain regulations and standards, auto-build compliance registers from uploaded documentation, run AI self-assessments with confidence-scored results, track regulatory submissions, manage incidents and breaches, and compare policies against requirements with AI remediation guidance.

As a multi-framework compliance software platform, Observeri maps controls and evidence across SAMA, NESA, ISO 27001, NIST CSF, DORA, MiCA, EU AI Act, SOC 2, and regional frameworks simultaneously — eliminating the duplication of maintaining separate compliance registers per standard. For enterprises, SMEs, and startups worldwide replacing spreadsheet compliance tracking, Observeri's automated regulatory compliance platform compresses compliance cycles from weeks to days, with compliance drift monitoring that alerts teams to control gaps before the next audit. It covers the regulatory regimes they work under.

faqs.question: What frameworks does Observeri Compliance Management support?
faqs.answer: Observeri supports SAMA Cybersecurity Framework, NESA, ISO 27001, NIST CSF, NIST 800-53, DORA, MiCA, EU AI Act, ISO 42001, SOC 2, PCI DSS, and additional regional standards — with the ability to add custom frameworks and map controls across multiple standards at once.

faqs.question: How does Observeri automate compliance management?
faqs.answer: Observeri auto-builds compliance registers from uploaded regulation documents, runs AI self-assessments with confidence scoring, tracks evidence collection against each control, monitors compliance drift, and generates audit-ready reports — reducing manual compliance effort significantly.

faqs.question: What is compliance drift and how does Observeri detect it?
faqs.answer: Compliance drift occurs when controls that were once effective become ineffective due to configuration changes, personnel changes, or evolving threats. Observeri monitors control effectiveness continuously and alerts teams when a previously passing control begins to degrade — before it becomes an audit finding.

/products/human-risk-management.title: Human Risk Management Platform | Insider Risk & Employee Cyber Risk Scoring
/products/human-risk-management.description: Observeri continuously profiles identities, monitors privileged accounts, and calculates Human Risk Exposure (HRE) scores — so teams act on the users driving the greatest cyber exposure.
/products/human-risk-management.h1: Human Risk Management — Quantify People Risk. AI Scans Privileged IDs Before Attackers Do.
body: Observeri Human Risk Management continuously profiles identities, monitors high-risk privileged accounts, and calculates Human Risk Exposure (HRE) scores using asset risk, privilege impact, access probability, trust factors, and environmental risk — so teams act on the users driving the greatest cyber exposure.

As an insider risk management software platform, Observeri goes beyond security awareness training metrics to quantify actual human risk. Employee security risk scoring gives security and GRC teams a ranked view of which identities represent the highest exposure — enabling targeted controls, access reviews, and monitoring. Human risk integrated with GRC means HRE scores feed the same risk register and remediation workflows as technical vulnerabilities, giving CISOs a complete picture of exposure across technology and people.

faqs.question: What is Human Risk Exposure (HRE)?
faqs.answer: Human Risk Exposure (HRE) is a quantified score that represents the risk an individual identity poses to the organisation, based on factors including asset access, privilege level, access probability, behavioural signals, and environmental risk. It enables teams to prioritise human-layer controls by actual risk rather than role or seniority alone.

faqs.question: How is Observeri's Human Risk Management different from security awareness platforms?
faqs.answer: Security awareness platforms track training completion and phishing simulation click rates. Observeri's Human Risk Management calculates a financial risk exposure score per identity based on actual access, behaviour, and environmental signals — integrating human risk into the same GRC risk register as technical vulnerabilities.

faqs.question: Does Observeri monitor privileged accounts specifically?
faqs.answer: Yes. Observeri continuously monitors high-risk privileged accounts — administrators, service accounts, and high-access users — scoring each for exposure and alerting when behaviour or access patterns suggest elevated risk, before an attacker can exploit that access.
